To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MetJ repressor binds to an 8 bp repeat site and represses transcription from the overlapping promoters of the metE (methionine synthase) and metR (methionine repressor) genes in Salmonella typhmurium.
the metE gene and the metR gene share a common operator region for MetJ-mediated regulation.
the metE-lactose and metR-gallactokinase genes share a common MetJ-mediated operator site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
regulation of the metE gene, which encodes a methionyl-tRNA formyltransferase.
the regulation of the metE (methionine synthase) and metR (met repressor) genes.
the regulation of genes that are involved in the synthesis of methionine and threonine in Salmonella typhurium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 8 bp repeats are required for MetJ binding, and that the metE-lacz promoter and the metR-gal promoter are repressed by MetJ through a shared operator site.
the metE gene is repressed by MetJ and that the metR gene is repressed and activated by MetJ and MetR, respectively.
the MetJ repressed operator site overlaps the -35 region for both the metR and metE genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MetR is a positive transcriptional regulator of its own gene, and that MetJ and MetR are negative transcriptional regulators of the metE gene, and that these genes are all under control by the same MetR/MetJ system.
MetJ-mediated regulation of both the metE and the metR genes occurs by binding to the same operator site.
the metE gene is regulated by the metR gene product, MetR, and the metE promoter is regulated by the MetJ-MetR repressor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metE-lactose and metR-gene fusions are repressed by the MetJ repressors.
the metE promoter overlaps with the metR promoter and they share a common operator.
we have identified a common operator region for the regulation of the metE gene and metR genes in Salmonella typhurium.
